groups.description: Live broad-category classifieds and recommerce platforms that this domain is modeled on — useful to see how buyer, seller, and merchant surfaces are positioned in practice.

links.title: OLX — global classifieds platform
links.relevance: The global classifieds leader and primary reference for the broad local-listings model spanning many categories.

links.title: Marktplaats (Adevinta, Netherlands)
links.relevance: A mature single-market general classifieds portal — good example of category breadth, casual-seller listing flow, and local buyer discovery.

references.label: Insight: Discovery quality matters more when trust is uncertain

links.title: eBay — recommerce benchmark
links.relevance: The global recommerce benchmark; shows professional-merchant storefronts, structured categories, and buyer trust mechanics at scale.

groups.description: Background on the classifieds / online-marketplace industry, its operators, and market structure.

links.title: Adevinta — about the classifieds portfolio
links.relevance: Explains the European multi-brand classifieds portfolio model that shapes how supply-side and ecosystem-partner segments are served.

links.title: OLX Group — newsroom
links.relevance: Primary-source updates on classifieds product strategy, category expansion, and trust initiatives across markets.

groups.description: How marketplaces frame buyer/seller safety and the regulations that govern third-party sellers.

links.title: FTC — INFORM Consumers Act: what online marketplaces need to know
links.relevance: Defines the seller-verification and disclosure obligations that drive the platform's trust controls and merchant-onboarding requirements.

links.title: FTC — what third-party sellers need to know (INFORM Consumers Act)
links.relevance: The seller-facing view of the same rules — relevant to the casual-seller and professional-merchant personas' onboarding and verification jobs.

groups.description: Resources aimed at professional sellers and the SaaS / feed-integration partners that supply listings programmatically.

links.title: eBay Developers Program
links.relevance: Example of the listing/inventory APIs and feed integrations that the merchant-SaaS and feed-integration partner persona builds against.

references.label: Job: Integrate once and operate reliably

groups.description: Free, social-graph and hyperlocal channels where casual sellers and buyers transact today — the substitutes a general listings marketplace competes with for low-friction local supply and demand.

links.title: Facebook Marketplace — Help Center
links.relevance: The dominant free social substitute for casual local selling; shows the zero-friction listing and Messenger-based negotiation flow the casual-seller persona expects.

links.title: Craigslist — list of local sites
links.relevance: The original city-scoped free classifieds model; a reference for how hyperlocal buyer discovery and minimal-trust listings still capture casual supply.

links.title: OfferUp — about
links.relevance: A mobile-first local recommerce substitute; illustrates in-app messaging, seller ratings, and local-pickup trust mechanics that shape buyer/seller expectations.

groups.description: Specialist EU vertical marketplaces (motors, real estate, jobs) whose deep category data and lead-generation models set the bar a horizontal platform must match in its top categories.

links.title: AutoScout24 — European automotive marketplace
links.relevance: Motors-vertical benchmark for structured vehicle attributes, dealer storefronts, and financing leads that the professional-merchant persona expects in the vehicles category.

links.title: ImmobilienScout24 — German real-estate marketplace
links.relevance: Real-estate-vertical reference for paid listing tiers and agent lead generation, informing how the property category and its professional sellers are served.

groups.description: Infrastructure providers for marketplace payments, payouts, and shipping — the rails that turn a listing into a completed, protected transaction for buyers and sellers.

links.title: Stripe Connect — payments for marketplaces and platforms
links.relevance: Reference architecture for split payments, seller payouts, and KYC onboarding that underpins the buyer-protection and merchant-payout capability areas.

links.title: Adyen for Platforms — marketplace payments documentation
links.relevance: Alternative EU-headquartered payments-platform stack covering balance accounts and payouts, relevant to the partner persona integrating settlement and escrow.

links.title: Shippo — multi-carrier shipping platform
links.relevance: Example of the shipping-label and tracking rails that let remote buyers and sellers fulfil orders, supporting the logistics/fulfilment capability area.

groups.description: EU-level rules that govern how the platform must handle content moderation, illegal listings, seller transparency, and ranking disclosure — the primary regulatory context for an EU-centric marketplace.

links.title: European Commission — Digital Services Act package
links.relevance: The official source for DSA obligations on illegal-content notice-and-action, trader traceability, and moderation transparency that drive the platform's trust-and-safety operations.

links.title: EUR-Lex — Platform-to-Business (P2B) Regulation (EU) 2019/1150
links.relevance: Binding rules on ranking transparency and fair terms for business users, directly shaping how search ranking and seller-facing terms are disclosed to the professional-merchant persona.
